items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: I worked with people like Don Costa for the first time

ctx.x: Do you feel that you had to have sort of — I’m not sure how to put this — like a different set of ears for when you had like the Lennon Sisters come in and then you had Peggy Lee, and then you had Cannonball, then you had a rock group.

No. You know as a studio engineer I worked at Capitol and I worked at RCA Victor before I really became an independent engineer. But that was a great training ground because I got to work with so many different artists. And you know it was a great training ground. And I worked with people like Don Costa for the first time and you know it was great. I went to work for Ode Records and I worked with Lou Adler a lot and I worked for A&M Records but Lou had an affiliation and had started Ode Records and whatever. And…

Yeah I can see that. They’re looking through the glass and they can be affected either way like if they see somebody on the other side of the glass shaking their head thinking uh oh, I’m not doing this right. In fact they could just be shaking their head about anything.
